dedupe_keys.name: telecom italia big data challenge mobile network activity of milan and trentino 2013 2014

description: The Telecom Italia Big Data Challenge released open datasets on urban life in the city of Milan and the Province of Trentino, described in a 2015 Scientific Data article by Barlacchi and colleagues. Its core telecommunications datasets are computed from the call detail records of the Telecom Italia mobile network: incoming and outgoing SMS, calls and internet traffic per square of a regular grid (about 235 metres in Milan) in ten-minute intervals, by country code, plus interaction matrices between grid squares and between the area and Italian provinces; the collection also has the grids, administrative regions, precipitation and weather station data, social media pulses, news and an electricity dataset of the Trentino distributor SET. Coverage: Milan and Trentino, 1 November 2013 to 1 January 2014. Format and access: 19 datasets on Harvard Dataverse (the Milan activity dataset alone has 62 daily text files, about 21 GB), free under the Open Database Licence 1.0 with attribution to the contest. Caveats: values are anonymised and rescaled activity counts, not users; two months only; the operator's market share is unknown per square. Simulation uses: demand and traffic patterns for mobile network capacity planning, population dynamics for hazard exposure, and benchmarks for traffic prediction. Related records: population estimates derived from these data are catalogued separately.
